::: {.page-header-block}

# Off the Clock

What keeps me occupied when I step away from code, compilers, and market tickers.

:::

::: {.hobby-section}

::: {.hobby-card}

![Gaming](../assets/images/gaming.jpg)

::: {.hobby-content}

**Gaming**

High-difficulty roguelikes, tight mechanics, and immersive single-player worlds. I like
games that respect player agency and reward deliberate execution—whether that's dialing
in a clean line in Trackmania, grinding heat runs in Hades, or exploring Nordic myth in
God of War.

**Favorites:** [God of War (2018)](https://www.metacritic.com/game/god-of-war/),
[Hades](https://www.metacritic.com/game/hades/),
[Trackmania](https://www.metacritic.com/game/trackmania/). **Co-op pick:**
[It Takes Two](https://www.metacritic.com/game/it-takes-two/).

:::

:::

::: {.hobby-card}

![Photography](../assets/images/photography.JPG)

::: {.hobby-content}

**Photography**

Shooting manual on a weathered Sony A6000 with prime lenses. Mostly architectural
geometry, brutalist concrete, harsh shadows, and quiet patches of forest. No heavy
retouching—just framing geometry and working with whatever light happens to be there.

:::

:::

::: {.hobby-card}

![History of Science and Mathematics](../assets/images/maths.JPG)

::: {.hobby-content}

**History of Science & Mathematics**

Fascinated by how messy real discoveries actually were. Breakthroughs rarely happen in a
clean eureka moment; they emerge from decades of dead ends, stubborn arguments, and
incremental groundwork laid by forgotten peers. Reading original papers keeps today's
software trends in perspective.

:::

:::

::: {.hobby-card}

![Cooking](../assets/images/cooking.jpg)

::: {.hobby-content}

**Cooking**

Mostly wok-tossed dinners, noodle bowls, and high-heat experiments. Big on fermentation
and sharp contrasts—mixing homemade kimchi into grilled cheese, tweaking chili crisp
ratios, or turning whatever is left in the fridge into a respectable fried rice.

:::

:::

::: {.hobby-card}

![Road Cycling](../assets/images/road_bike.jpg)

::: {.hobby-content}

**Road Cycling**

Riding a restored 90s steel-frame road bike. No power meters, cadence sensors, or
electronic shifting—just friction shifters, skinny tires, and long weekend rides on
quiet asphalt.

:::

:::

::: {.hobby-card}

![Strolling](../assets/images/strolling.jpg)

::: {.hobby-content}

**Strolling**

Daily walks without headphones, podcasts, or a fitness tracker buzzing on my wrist. The
easiest way to untangle architectural knots in a codebase, shake off screen fatigue, and
reset focus.

:::

:::

:::
